title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Copyright

articles.content_en:
Article 2 Copyright civil dispute cases shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Courts at or above the intermediate level.
Each Higher People's Court may, based on the actual circumstances within its jurisdiction, apply to the Supreme People's Court for approval to have certain Primary People's Courts exercise jurisdiction over first-instance copyright civil dispute cases.

Article 3 Where a party initiates a prosecution before the People's Court to pursue the civil liability of the person who committed an act of copyright infringement that has been investigated and dealt with by the copyright administrative department, the People's Court shall accept the case.
When trying a civil dispute case involving an act of copyright infringement that has already been handled by the copyright administrative department, the People's Court shall conduct a comprehensive review of the facts of the case.

Article 5 For a joint action brought against multiple defendants whose infringing acts were committed in different places, the plaintiff may choose to bring a prosecution before the People's Court at the place where one of the defendants committed the infringing act;
for an action brought only against one of the defendants, the People's Court at the place where that defendant committed the infringing act shall have jurisdiction.

Article 6 Where a copyright collective management organization lawfully established, upon written authorization from the copyright owner, brings a prosecution in its own name, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 7 Manuscripts, originals, lawful publications, copyright registration certificates, certificates issued by certification institutions, contracts for obtaining rights, and other materials involving copyright provided by a party may serve as evidence.
A natural person, legal person, or unincorporated organization named on a work or product shall be deemed the owner of copyright or rights related to copyright, unless there is contrary proof.

Article 8 Physical objects, invoices, and other items obtained by a party through purchasing infringing copies by itself or through an authorized agent by means such as ordering or on-site transaction may serve as evidence.
A notarial certificate issued by a notary who, without disclosing identity to the party suspected of infringement, truthfully certifies the evidence obtained by the other party in accordance with the method prescribed in the preceding paragraph and the process of obtaining such evidence, shall be used as evidence, unless there is contrary evidence.

Article 9 "Making available to the public" as provided in Item (1) of Article 10 of the Copyright Law means that a copyright owner, by itself or with the permission of the copyright owner, discloses the work to unspecified persons, but public awareness is not a constitutive element.

Article 10 For a work referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 15 of the Copyright Law, if the copyright owner is a natural person, the term of protection shall be governed by the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 21 of the Copyright Law;
if the copyright owner is a legal person or an unincorporated organization, the term of protection shall be governed by the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 21 of the Copyright Law.

Article 12 Where, pursuant to Article 17 of the Copyright Law, the copyright in a commissioned work belongs to the commissioned party, the commissioning party shall enjoy the right to use the work within the agreed scope of use;
if the parties have not agreed on the scope of use of the work, the commissioning party may use the work free of charge within the specific purpose of the commissioned creation.

Article 13 Except for the circumstances provided in paragraph 3 of Article 11 of the Copyright Law, for a report, speech, or other work written by another person, reviewed and finalized by the principal, and published in the principal's name, the copyright shall be enjoyed by the reporter or speaker.
The copyright owner may pay appropriate remuneration to the writer.

Article 14 Where the parties jointly agree to complete an autobiographical work based on the experiences of a specific person, if the parties have an agreement on the ownership of copyright, the agreement shall prevail;
if there is no agreement, the copyright shall be enjoyed by the specific person, and where the writer or compiler has contributed labor to the completion of the work, the copyright owner may pay appropriate remuneration to him or her.

Article 15 Where works on the same subject matter are created by different authors, if the expression of the works is independently completed and original, each author shall be deemed to enjoy independent copyright.

Article 16 Pure factual information disseminated through mass media constitutes current news as provided in Item (2) of Article 5 of the Copyright Law.
Where current news gathered and edited by others is disseminated or reported, the source shall be indicated.

Article 17 Reprinting as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 33 of the Copyright Law refers to the act of a newspaper or periodical publishing a work that has already been published in another newspaper or periodical.
If a reprint fails to indicate the author of the reprinted work and the source of the newspaper or periodical in which it was initially published, the reprinting party shall bear civil liability such as eliminating the consequences and making an apology.

Article 18 Art works in outdoor public places as provided in Item (10) of Article 22 of the Copyright Law refer to art works such as sculptures, paintings, and calligraphy installed or displayed in places of outdoor social activities of the public.
A person who copies, paints, photographs, or video-records the art works provided in the preceding paragraph may use the results again in a reasonable manner and within a reasonable scope, and such use does not constitute infringement.

Article 19 Publishers and producers shall bear the burden of adducing evidence that they have lawful authorization for their publication or production, and distributors and lessors shall bear the burden of adducing evidence that the copies they distribute or lease have a lawful source.
If they are unable to adduce evidence, they shall bear legal liability in accordance with the corresponding provisions of Articles 47 and 48 of the Copyright Law.

Article 20 Where a publication infringes upon another person's copyright, the publisher shall bear liability for damages based on its fault, the degree of infringement, the consequences of damage, and other factors.
If the publisher fails to fulfill its reasonable duty of care with respect to the authorization for the publication act, the source and authorship of the manuscript, the content of the edited publication, and other matters, it shall bear liability for damages in accordance with Article 49 of the Copyright Law.
The publisher shall bear the burden of adducing evidence that it has fulfilled its reasonable duty of care.

Article 21 Where a computer software user commercially uses computer software without permission or beyond the scope of permission, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with Item (1) of Article 48 of the Copyright Law and Item (1) of Article 24 of the Regulations on the Protection of Computer Software.
Article 22 Where a copyright transfer contract is not made in writing, the People's Court shall examine whether the contract is established pursuant to Article 490 of the Civil Code.

Article 23 Where a publisher loses or damages the work delivered for publication by the copyright owner, causing the publication contract to be incapable of performance, the copyright owner shall have the right to require the publisher to bear corresponding civil liability in accordance with Articles 186, 238, and 1184 of the Civil Code and other provisions.

Article 24 The actual loss of the right holder may be calculated based on the decrease in the number of copies distributed by the right holder caused by the infringement, or based on the product of the number of infringing copies sold and the unit profit of the right holder from distributing such copies.
If the decrease in the number of copies distributed is difficult to determine, it shall be determined according to the market sales volume of the infringing copies.

Article 25 Where the actual loss of the right holder or the unlawful gains of the infringer cannot be determined, the People's Court shall, at the request of a party or on its own authority, apply the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 49 of the Copyright Law to determine the amount of damages.
When determining the amount of damages, the People's Court shall consider the type of work, reasonable license fee, nature of the infringing act, consequences, and other circumstances in a comprehensive manner.
Where the parties reach an agreement on the amount of damages in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article, the agreement shall be permitted.

Article 26 The reasonable expenses paid to stop the infringing act as provided in paragraph 1 of Article 49 of the Copyright Law include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder or the authorized agent in investigating and obtaining evidence of the infringing act.
The People's Court may, based on the litigation claims of the parties and the specific circumstances of the case, include the attorney's fees that comply with the provisions of the relevant state authorities in the scope of damages.

Article 28 Where the People's Court takes preservation measures, it shall handle the matter in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Review of Behavioral Preservation Cases Involving Intellectual Property Disputes.
Article 30 Where the previous relevant provisions are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
